correctness.rationale: The signed batch imbalance has exact first and second moments 0 and 1/η. Squaring the explicit coordinate update gives B exactly. Positivity of B yields a simple Perron root controlling every deterministic nonzero initial error, radical diagonalization gives r, and the determinant crossing plus strict convexity proves the exact mean-square frontier and sharp boundaries. The separate conditional energy operator yields the one-step threshold and strict gap. Convexity and signed derivatives at 1 and 2 give unique optimal alpha; exhaustive exact rational path enumeration across three finite steps passed 1,116 equalities.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: One-step strict contraction implies stability but not conversely; algebraically the one-step frontier is 4/(1+ρ+(1-ρ)/η), while true mean-square frontier is 4/(1+sqrt(ρ²+(1-ρ²)/η²)), strictly larger at 0<ρ<1 and η>1. An upper bound optimized in the former source results does not logically imply the new exact operator/optimal asymptotic parameter. The established exact-MSE lifting is acknowledged as method precedent.

originality.rationale: Direct comparison of the exact long-run second-moment operator and separate conditional one-step bound shows a substantive, nontrivial distinction. Inspected primary averaged-Kaczmarz articles establish algorithms and conservative guarantee tuning but no exact two-row annealed Perron formula. Exact-MSE machinery is classical and credited; scientific novelty is the sharp coexistence window and complete two-row rate. Related published records concern different recurrence mechanisms. Residual priority risk remains for uninspected appendices and older exact-MSE works.
residual_risks: The complete BIT journal text and some original 2014 exact-MSE manuscript pages were inaccessible; a narrowly equivalent special-case derivation might exist there.

The published-result record comparisons were statement-level rather than comprehensive document inspections; independent priority review is not performed.

value.rationale: The sharp nonempty gap between conditional stepwise monotonicity and actual long-run mean-square stability directly addresses conservative fixed-step tuning in independently averaged row solvers. It is a structural distinction with explicit endpoints for every pair of nonorthogonal normalized rows and every finite batch; convergence of averages of individually isometric reflections at relaxation 2 is an illuminating nontrivial consequence, not merely a generic one-step bound.
